title: Reverse Exchange Coordination
name: Reverse Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Reverse Exchange Coordination in Phoenix, AZ
metaDescription: Coordinating reverse 1031 exchanges in Phoenix when a strong replacement property closes before your relinquished sale, using an accommodation titleholder.

sections.html: Sometimes the right building shows up before your current property is sold. In Phoenix's faster-moving submarkets that happens more than investors expect, and a reverse exchange is the structure built for exactly that situation.

sections.heading: Why Phoenix Deals Push Investors Into a Reverse
sections.html: West Valley industrial sites tied to the growth around Loop 303 and new multifamily in the outer submarkets can move from listing to under-contract in days, not weeks. If your relinquished property isn't sold yet when a property like that comes available, a standard forward exchange won't work because you'd own the replacement before selling the old one.

sections.heading: How the Structure Actually Works
sections.html: An exchange accommodation titleholder, set up under a qualified exchange accommodation agreement, takes and holds title to either the replacement or the relinquished property while you sort out the other side of the transaction. Your qualified intermediary and the accommodation titleholder coordinate the parking arrangement; you never hold both properties directly at the same time in a way that breaks the structure.

sections.heading: What Has to Happen, In Order
sections.html:
Coordinating a reverse exchange means keeping several pieces moving on parallel tracks:

  • Engage the qualified intermediary and exchange accommodation titleholder before the replacement property closes
  • Draft the qualified exchange accommodation agreement covering the parked property
  • Arrange financing that works with a title-holding entity rather than you directly
  • Set a target timeline for selling the relinquished property or completing the exchange
  • Confirm identification and closing deadlines that run from the parking date

Financing is usually the tightest piece, since not every lender is set up to underwrite a loan to an accommodation titleholder.

sections.heading: The Deadlines Don't Change Just Because the Order Flipped
sections.html:
A reverse exchange still runs against a one-hundred-eighty-day outside limit and a forty-five-day identification window, just measured from the parking date instead of a relinquished sale closing. We track both dates from day one so the accommodation structure gets unwound on schedule.

We coordinate the moving pieces; your qualified intermediary and CPA confirm the exchange structure and tax treatment fit your situation.

sections.heading: Where This Gets Expensive If Rushed
sections.html: Reverse exchanges cost more to set up than a standard forward exchange, mostly in accommodation titleholder fees and financing complexity. We flag that cost early so you can weigh it against losing a Phoenix property you'd otherwise miss while waiting to sell.

sections.heading: A Typical Sequence We've Coordinated
sections.html:
On a recent West Valley industrial parking arrangement, the investor's relinquished property, an older retail center, was under contract but hadn't closed when a well-located building near Loop 303 came available. The accommodation titleholder took title to the replacement, the industrial building, while the retail sale worked through its own closing timeline over the following weeks. Once the retail sale closed, the exchange completed and title to the industrial building transferred to the investor.

That sequence only worked because financing on the parked property was arranged with a lender comfortable lending to the accommodation titleholder structure from the start, not scrambled together after the parking arrangement was already signed.

sections.heading: Questions to Settle Before You Commit to This Structure
sections.html: Before recommending a reverse exchange over waiting for a standard sale-then-purchase sequence, we walk through how confident the relinquished property sale actually is, how the financing on the parked property will work, and what the accommodation titleholder's fee structure looks like for the specific timeline involved. Those answers usually make clear whether the reverse structure is worth it for a given property or whether it makes more sense to let the current listing sell first.

sections.heading: Why Title Companies Take Longer on These Closings
sections.html: Maricopa County title companies generally need extra lead time on a reverse exchange closing, since the accommodation titleholder entity has to be added to the title commitment and the closing documents drafted for an entity that isn't you personally. We loop in the title company as soon as a reverse structure looks likely, not after the purchase contract is already signed, so that extra drafting time doesn't threaten your closing date.

sections.heading: What This Costs Compared to Waiting
sections.html: We put a real number in front of investors before they choose this path: accommodation titleholder fees, added legal drafting, and any financing premium, weighed against the risk of losing a specific Phoenix property to another buyer while a relinquished sale finishes closing. Some properties are worth that cost; a lot aren't, and the honest answer depends on how replaceable that specific building actually is in the current market.

faqs.q: When does a reverse exchange make sense for a Phoenix property?
faqs.a: When a strong replacement property is available now but your relinquished property hasn't sold yet. Fast-moving submarkets like West Valley industrial are where we see this come up most often.

faqs.q: What is an exchange accommodation titleholder?
faqs.a: An entity that holds title to either the replacement or relinquished property temporarily, under a qualified exchange accommodation agreement, while the rest of the exchange gets sorted out. Your qualified intermediary sets this up.

faqs.q: Do the 45-day and 180-day deadlines still apply to a reverse exchange?
faqs.a: Yes, generally measured from the date the property is parked with the accommodation titleholder rather than from a relinquished sale closing. We track both dates from the start.

faqs.q: Is financing harder to arrange in a reverse exchange?
faqs.a: Often, yes, since the loan may need to go to the accommodation titleholder rather than to you directly. We flag this early so financing isn't the piece that stalls the deal.

faqs.q: Why do reverse exchanges cost more than a standard exchange?
faqs.a: Accommodation titleholder fees and the added legal and financing complexity add cost compared to a forward exchange. We lay out that cost before you decide whether the structure is worth it for a specific property.
